conviction_note: Small up lean (p_up 56). Halliburton's Q3 print the same morning showed Middle East/Asia up 8% on Saudi Arabia and Kuwait and Mexico activity higher. Those are the two lines that drove WFRD's Q2 decline. Offsetting them is a renewed Hormuz disruption in early October, a risk to the Q4/2027 guide. abs_move 6.5% sits between the 7.42% event-implied move and the 4.15% median reaction. Findings sum +0.6, scaled +0.78; the two measurements agree in sign and size.

positioning_check: Short interest ~5.9M shares, ~3.9 days to cover as of the 2026-07-15 FINRA settlement (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/wfrd/short-interest/). Equibles shows ~8% of float (https://equibles.com/stocks/wfrd/shortinterest). Not crowded, and no newer settlement was found. Skew 25d is -0.83 vol pts (balanced, a slight call bid). Put/call OI is 0.85, but total OI is only 493 and the ATM spread is 31% of mid, so the chain is thin. The stock fell from $98.72 (2026-09-02, Benzinga) to $78.55 at the seal: -20% in seven weeks, 20d run-up -6.49%, 29.5% off the 52w high. Sell-side was 11 Buy/1 Hold, avg PT $126 (https://es.benzinga.com/quote/WFRD/analyst-ratings).

findings.finding: Halliburton's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-20) shows Middle East/Asia revenue $1.4B, +8% q/q, 'driven by higher activity in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait', and international revenue +3% q/q. WFRD's MENA/Asia region is ~40% of revenue ($446M in Q2) and fell 6% q/q in Q2 on the Iran conflict. WFRD's own Q3 guide (revenue $1.105-1.155B, flat to +4.5% q/q) was set when it called Kuwait among the 'most disrupted' markets.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: MENA -6% q/q and EPS $0.55 vs ~$0.93 consensus, yet the stock reacted +4.55%. 6 of the last 7 prints reacted up (median |move| 4.15%); the one big down was -7.18% in Apr-2025.
findings.why_not_priced: HAL released the morning of the seal day and the seal is at 12:01 ET, so part of this is in the price. WFRD's 5d run-up is only +1.74%, and the 20d is -6.49% in a stock 20% below its early-September level. If the market had moved WFRD's Q3 bar to the top of the guide, the stock would have bounced off its lows on the day. Net of the rest of the company: WFRD warned Saudi revenue falls in H2 as its LSTK contract ends. That partly offsets a Saudi activity pickup, so the size is held below a full MENA read.
findings.independence: Same company's peer data only. WFRD itself said on 2026-07-22 that Saudi Arabia and the UAE were recovering and the Middle East impact was 'moderating' (https://www.webull.com/news/15271277430924288).

findings.finding: The same Halliburton Q3 release reports Latin America revenue flat q/q at $1.12B, with 'Mexico: higher activity across multiple product service lines'. WFRD's Latin America revenue fell 12% q/q in Q2 to $197M, mainly on lower Mexico drilling services and integrated projects. On 2026-07-22 WFRD said it expected the Pemex calendar to normalise in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 Latin America -12% q/q on Mexico; the stock still reacted +4.55%. No separate history for the Mexico line.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a counterparty read-through published hours before the seal, in a peer release whose headline was flat revenue. Latin America is ~18% of WFRD revenue, so the effect is small. If it were priced, WFRD would have outperformed on the day of HAL's release, which the 5d +1.74% does not show.
findings.independence: Same document as the Middle East finding, so the two share one source. WFRD management (2026-07-22) expected the H2 Pemex calendar to normalise: https://www.webull.com/news/15271277430924288

findings.finding: Weatherford completed its NCS Multistage acquisition on 2026-09-01, so Q3 carries one month of NCS revenue. NCS's annual revenue is roughly $160-170M (my estimate, not in the release), or ~$14M a month. The Q3 revenue guide ($1.105-1.155B) was given on 2026-07-22, before closing, which tilts reported revenue toward the upper half of the guide if the guide excluded NCS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior acquisition-month print in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Whether consensus models the NCS stub is unclear. Benzinga's $1.13B sits exactly at the guide midpoint, which suggests it does not. The effect is about 1% of revenue and mostly mechanical, so the size is small. The deal was predominantly paid in equity, which adds shares, so the per-share effect is roughly neutral.
findings.independence: Q2 call: the deal was expected to close in H2 with mostly equity consideration and >=$15M synergies (https://www.webull.com/news/15271277430924288)

findings.finding: Hormuz disruption re-escalated in early October 2026. Strait transits fell to 4 on 2026-10-04 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 a day, the lowest in over two months. A tanker was struck off Qatar on 2026-10-07 and Iran warned it would block unauthorised routes. In July WFRD named Qatar, Bahrain, Iraq and Kuwait as its most disrupted markets and said the impact would not reach zero without a permanent resolution. That makes the Q4 guide and the 2027 'growth year' commentary the risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Apr-2025 print -7.18% (a guidance cut in a tariff/oil sell-off). Q2 2026 'slightly reduced' FY outlook was still bought, +4.55%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is -20% since 2026-09-02 while Brent is above $100. The size is below a full guide-cut scale for that reason. What is not priced is how WFRD quantifies the October flare-up for Q4; it had only 'incorporated the recent flare-up' as of July. This is macro-to-company transmission the company has not yet confirmed for Q4, so it is filed as a proxy.
findings.independence: Proxy. HAL's Q3 release (same day) gives no Middle East outlook and calls the period 'one of the largest energy disruptions in history': https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000045012/000004501226000070/livemastererdocument.htm

findings.finding: The US rig count rose for a third straight week to 599 in the week to 2026-09-25, its highest since May 2024 (oil rigs 455). WFRD's North America is ~19% of revenue ($205M in Q2, -7% q/q on Canadian breakup), and US land artificial lift grew in Q2. NCS's completions business adds further North American exposure.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a public industry series, so it is largely priced. It is filed small as an industry proxy. HAL, by contrast, reported North America down 5% q/q on US land pressure pumping, a product line WFRD barely has.
findings.independence: Mixed: HAL Q3 North America -5% q/q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000045012/000004501226000070/livemastererdocument.htm)

findings.finding: Petroleum Development Oman awarded Weatherford a three-year integrated drilling services contract covering 274 wells in Marmul and the Greater Saqr Area (Block 6), reported by MEED on 2026-09-23. It lands after the Q2 call and supports the backlog and 2027 growth commentary on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Contract awards are routinely listed in WFRD releases; no measured reaction to them.
findings.why_not_priced: The award ran in a paywalled trade publication with no company press release found, and the stock kept falling after it. Its value is unquantified, so the size is small. Oman is a market WFRD called 'stable'.

findings.finding: Pemex's H1 2026 SEC filing deferred MXN 255.4bn of recognised supplier debt to 2033, ~68% of its MXN 374bn supplier obligations (reported 2026-08-26). Separately, the Banobras supplier-payment fund was exhausted by May 2026. WFRD's Q3 adj. FCF guide of '>$100M' names Mexico collections as the main source of variability.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 FCF was strong ($139M, +64% q/q) and the stock reacted +4.55% despite an EPS miss, so this name pays for the FCF line.
findings.why_not_priced: The Mexican press covers Pemex's supplier deferrals; US sell-side previews focus on the Middle East. It is a proxy for WFRD's own receivables, and the company was only 'cautiously optimistic' on H2 collections. It is filed small because WFRD's FCF guide already allowed for Mexico variability.
findings.independence: Amespac (oil services suppliers' association) said on 2026-07-08 that the Pemex payment fund was exhausted and 2024 work remains unpaid: https://www.elimparcial.com/mexico/2026/07/08/proveedores-de-pemex-acusaron-que-el-fondo-para-pagarles-se-acabo/

baseline_tension: The skew is balanced (-0.83) and the stock has been sold 20% since early September, so a small up lean from peer read-through does not fight the options market. The Hormuz guide risk cuts the other way and is partly what the drawdown already holds.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): the HAL Middle East finding was cut from +1.2 to +1.0, because WFRD's Saudi LSTK roll-off partly offsets a Saudi activity pickup.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the revenue/EBITDA bar is confirmed against the company guide plus Benzinga. The EPS bar is disputed ($1.20 vs $1.26 vs an implied ~$1.0), so nothing is sized on EPS.
Lesson 7: short interest was checked before the Hormuz negative. Not crowded (~3.9 days), so that finding was left at -1.5.
Lesson 1 (reaction history): 6 of 7 prints were up, including on an EPS miss, so p_up and the lean were left as they were. Nothing else changed.
